subject: Renewal structure + safety-net options for FY27
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Jordan <lisa@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal structure + safety-net options for FY27

Hi Lisa —

Following up from our QBR: I sketched three straightforward renewal structures that typically help teams balance predictability vs. flexibility. Attached is a short checklist (renewal_safety_net_checklist.pdf) so your procurement and finance folks can see the operational steps. High level: 

1) 24-month multi-year with phased ramp (preferred)
   - Year 1: 60% of committed capacity, Year 2: 100%
   - True-up at Q4 of Year 1 with a capped true-up band (±15%)

2) 12-month + auto-renew (simpler ops)
   - Auto-renew opt-in with 30-day cancellation window before renewal

3) Flex-first (usage + reserved burst)
   - Lower committed floor, burst buffer, convert-to-annual at milestone

Other options: frontloaded credits if you want to accelerate onboarding, and a triggerline safety-net — an agreed buffer that gives Acme temporary burst capacity without immediate contract change while we true-up usage.

Would you be available for 30 minutes next week to pick one? If so, I can send a short mutual action plan and a draft amendment for legal.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0124
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: renewal_safety_net_checklist.pdf

From: Lisa Jordan <lisa@acmecloud.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal structure + safety-net options for FY27

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear options. We prefer the 24-month multi-year with phased ramp but need a firm escape hatch at the 12-month mark (we're planning a product re-architecture in Q2 of FY27). Also want clearer language on early-exit true-up and whether frontloaded credits can be applied to Year 2 if we hit onboarding delays.

Can you share a sample amendment + the pricing impact for the 2-year structure (with and without credits)? Looping in procurement on cc — they will review redlines.

Best,
Lisa Jordan
Head of Cloud Partnerships | Acme Cloud

Subject: Re: Renewal structure + safety-net options for FY27

Lisa / team —

Appreciate the quick feedback. Attached is draft_amendment_v1.docx (high level) and a short mutual action plan below. Pricing scenarios summarized after the MAP.

Mutual action plan (proposed)
- Week 1: Agree on term (2yr) + ramp %
- Week 2: Legal redlines on draft amendment (we'll accept limited early-exit language with true-up band)
- Week 3: Finalize DocuSign and schedule onboarding kickoff with Marissa

Proposed canary ramp schedule (operationally friendly)
- Month 0–3: Onboard (no commit billing for initial dev environment)
- Month 4–9: 60% committed throughput
- Month 10–12: 80% commit (true-up assessment at month 12)
- Year 2: 100% commit

Pricing (illustrative)
- 2yr with no credits: baseline list * 0.94 (4% multi-year uplift discount)
- 2yr with frontloaded onboarding credits: baseline * 0.90 + $75k onboarding credit applied in quarter 1

Escape hatch language we recommend: "Either party may initiate a true-up review at the 12-month anniversary. If usage deviates from the agreed ramp by more than ±15%, both parties will engage to agree an amended capacity schedule. If no agreement is reached within 30 days, the customer may elect a one-time partial termination with a pro-rata settlement equal to unused committed capacity less onboarding credits applied."

Link to DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/unsigned/ACME-2026

If that language looks acceptable, I'll ask legal to incorporate a short clause and circulate. Marissa — can you confirm we'll be able to set the Dedicated burst window for their onboarding as described?

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments: draft_amendment_v1.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Jordan <lisa@acmecloud.com>, Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal structure + safety-net options for FY27

Thanks Karthik — quick ops notes from my side: 

- We can reserve a burst pool for the onboarding quarter (up to 30% above committed capped at a fixed token budget).
- Ops runbook will include a pre-warm window and a KV-cache priming checklist to reduce token cost spikes. I've attached an initial ops_runbook.xlsx for your SREs.
- SLO credits: per the SLA, we can offer a 5% credit to monthly invoice for sustained latency breaches >3 consecutive days — we should call this out in the amendment if Acme deems it important.

Lisa — from an implementation perspective the canary ramp above is good; it gives us predictable forecasting while still providing operational breathing room. If procurement wants to see a sample invoice cadence, I can generate a projected burn schedule for Year 1.

Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: ops_runbook.xlsx

From: Acme Cloud Procurement <procurement@acmecloud.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal structure + safety-net options for FY27

Karthik / Marissa —

We reviewed draft_amendment_v1.docx internally and have redlines (see attached redlines_acme.pdf). Two asks: 

1) We want explicit language that frontloaded credits cannot be clawed back if onboarding is delayed through no fault of Acme (we will accept a pro-rata adjustment otherwise).
2) The escape hatch needs to include a true-up arbitration path (third-party arbitrator) if parties cannot agree within 30 days.

Also, please confirm the invoice cadence and whether credits apply to tax calculations. We will have legal loop in our counsel for a call early next week.

Regards,
Acme Cloud Procurement (on behalf of Tom Huang)
procurement@acmecloud.com
